entities.summary: Equine-assisted therapy (EAT) encompasses a range of treatments that involve activities with horses and other equines to promote human physical and mental health. Modern use of horses for mental health treatment dates to the 1990s. Systematic review of studies of EAT as applied to physical health date only to about 2007, and a lack of common terminology and standardization has caused problems with meta-analysis. Due to a lack of high-quality studies assessing the efficacy of equine-assisted therapies for mental health treatment, concerns have been raised that these therapies should not replace or divert resources from other evidence-based mental health therapies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Therapeutic horseback riding has had a significant impact on mental health treatment since its modern use in the 1990s, with studies suggesting it can improve symptoms of anxiety and depression. While its efficacy is still being studied, EAT has become a widely accepted treatment option for individuals with mental health conditions.
